title: Impact of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (research review)
text: Broad review of SBM's first decade, covering sanitation and municipal waste management alongside urban population growth. Does not reach a firm conclusion on success or failure; argues the evidence base is still thin and calls for better longitudinal data before firm conclusions are drawn.

title: Swachh Bharat Mission: A Case Study
text: Case study of one sub-division in Assam covering the mission's objectives, local implementation strategy, and the gap between the two. Public health and environmental outcomes were mixed rather than clearly positive or negative.

title: Impacts of SBM on Health and Communicable Disease Control (systematic review protocol)
text: A protocol, not a finished study, setting out how the authors plan to systematically review SBM's effect on communicable disease. States that despite international praise for the mission, its health impact has not yet been rigorously established. The review will draw on major medical databases and grey literature.

title: Financial and Economic Impacts of the Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin)
text: UNICEF-led cost-benefit analysis for the Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation. Finds that SBM(G) pays for itself: even households funding their own toilet (about INR 16,000) recover the cost in about two years through medical savings. The estimate is conservative because it excludes some sanitation-linked diseases and stunting effects.

title: A Study on Implication of Swachh Bharat among Students
text: Student paper with a generally favourable tone. Cites WHO's figure of about 180,000 averted diarrhoeal deaths and an Ashoka University finding linking toilet construction to fewer reported sexual assaults on women. References NFHS data on sanitation access and identifies ongoing gaps in public transport sanitation for students.

title: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan: SWOT Analysis
source_name: ResearchGate / Int J Community Med Public Health
text: SWOT analysis of the mission. Strengths: visibility and CSR funding channels. Main weakness: participation is voluntary rather than compulsory, so there is no enforcement mechanism. Recommends stronger awareness and enforcement mechanisms.

title: Effectiveness of the Swachh Bharat Mission and barriers to ending open defecation (systematic review)
text: Systematic review of studies from 13 states (mainly UP, Bihar, MP, Rajasthan and Maharashtra) on what worked and what did not in ending open defecation. Finds that effectiveness varied widely by region and by how each study defined success, so SBM's impact cannot be treated as uniform nationwide.

title: Swachh Bharat Mission - Current Affairs Briefing
text: Exam-preparation briefing. Reports that the budget allocation fell from about 16,000 crore (2017-18) to about 7,000 crore (2024-25), and that spending on awareness campaigns also fell. Notes new sanitation-worker welfare initiatives announced for the mission's 10th anniversary.

title: The Reality of the Swachh Bharat Mission
text: Editorial arguing that India's overall environmental performance remains weak despite SBM's scale, that toilet construction quality has been substandard, and that the mission has not broken from caste-based sanitation labour. Groups SBM with AMRUT, PMAY and NCAP as ambitious programmes that fall short of their goals.

title: Why the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan Failed
text: Opinion piece arguing that public sanitation habits have not meaningfully changed years after launch, citing continued littering and open defecation. Places some blame on citizens but most on the government's lack of follow-through on maintenance.

title: How the Swachh Bharat Mission is heading for failure
text: Long investigative piece tracing SBM from its 2014 launch. Argues that promises such as ending manual scavenging were being broken even as the political machinery continued to promote the campaign, and documents the gap between official messaging and ground reality.

title: The failure of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan: we need a better way to manage trash
text: Opinion piece arguing that visible cleanliness has not improved much relative to the money and ambition invested. Argues that waste collection and toilet upkeep are government responsibilities that citizen messaging campaigns alone cannot fix.

title: Swachh Bharat has made little difference, govt should factor in criticism
text: Response to another op-ed. Argues that SBM is not very different in practice from earlier sanitation policies and objects to the shame-based and gendered messaging around toilet use. Calls on the government to take criticism seriously instead of treating targets met as success.

title: PM Modi addresses Swachhata Hi Seva 2024 programme
source_name: All India Radio / News on Air (government press release)
text: Official release with 10th-anniversary framing, presenting cleanliness as a lifelong commitment rather than a one-off. Reports 27+ lakh events and 28 crore participants over the 'Seva Pakhwada' fortnight, credits sanitation workers, NGOs and celebrities, and announces about 10,000 crore in new cleanliness infrastructure.

title: Union Minister C R Patil urges people to undertake Shramdaan for Swachhata
source_name: All India Radio / News on Air (government press release)
text: Anniversary release about a nationwide voluntary cleaning hour. Reports that 38+ lakh Safai Mitras are now part of the campaign and describes the mission's progress as a shift from ODF status toward expanded solid and liquid waste management.

title: India rejects UN official's criticism (manual scavenging and caste)
text: A UN special rapporteur said the rights of lower-caste sanitation workers were being violated by their continued role in cleaning SBM-built toilets; the government publicly rejected this. Activists quoted say manual scavenging has not ended and may have worsened where toilets are not properly connected to water or sewage.

title: One Death Every Few Days: Sanitation Workers Protest at Jantar Mantar
text: Covers a 2026 Safai Karmachari Andolan protest. Its count is 593 sewer and septic-tank deaths between January 2021 and July 2026, higher than the government's own figure. Families of the deceased and MPs attended, and protesters demanded that the Prime Minister publicly take responsibility for the failure.

title: Nearly 500 sewer, septic tank cleaning deaths since 2019, Centre tells Lok Sabha
text: Government's parliamentary figure: about 498 deaths from 2019 to mid-2026 despite the legal ban on manual cleaning. The Supreme Court issued contempt notices to five states for not complying with its 2023 directions. SBM-Urban 2.0 includes a mechanisation push intended to address this.

title: 52 Sanitation Workers Lost Lives Due to Hazardous Cleaning in a Year
text: Reports a cumulative 471 deaths since 2019, mostly from toxic gas inhalation. Describes the NAMASTE scheme, which provides safety training and PPE and states a goal of zero fatalities through mechanisation.

title: India's Sewer Death Crisis: Why Fatalities Don't Count as Manual Scavenging
text: Argues that none of the roughly 500 recorded deaths have been officially classified as manual-scavenging-related, which avoids accountability. Blames outsourcing to contractors who escape monitoring, and quotes the view that responsibility is denied 'until a death brings attention.'

title: Swachh Survekshan 2025: Indore cleanest city for 8th consecutive year
text: Indore named India's cleanest city for the 8th consecutive year, with Surat and Navi Mumbai close behind; the President presented the awards. Officials linked the results to the 'Viksit Bharat 2047' development narrative.

title: CAG report flags irregularities in Uttar Pradesh's waste management
text: Audit covering 2016-22 in Uttar Pradesh. Findings: delayed fund releases, violations of contract-award rules that benefited private firms, and low urgency from urban local bodies on solid waste management.

title: CAG flags procurement deficiencies in Delhi's waste management under SBM
text: Procurement audit findings for Delhi: delayed funds, capital grants spent on truck rentals instead of approved purposes, materials ordered without confirming storage space, and compensation improperly withheld on delayed supplies.

title: CAG audit flags Assam government's failure to utilize SWM funds
text: Assam's urban local bodies left tens of crores allocated for solid waste management unused between 2018 and 2022. The state allocated less than its own finance commission recommended, and the central ministry did not release funds during the audit period, a failure at multiple levels.

title: Not a single toilet built in Delhi under Swachh Bharat Mission, CAG report says
text: Reports that no toilets were built in Delhi more than two years after launch, with about 40 crore lying idle in banks due to disbursal delays. The areas most lacking toilets, unauthorised colonies, were excluded from targeting from the start.

title: ED probes BBMP for misusing Swachh Bharat funds in Bengaluru
text: Enforcement Directorate money-laundering probe: about 92 crore of SBM grants allegedly diverted by Bengaluru's municipal corporation to road, footpath and drain work instead of sanitation, reportedly with elected officials involved.

title: Understanding Open Defecation in the Age of SBM: rural Bihar ethnography
text: Ethnographic fieldwork in rural Bihar. Challenges the assumption that people avoid latrines because they prefer open defecation; residents were well aware of the risks. Larger factors were subsidy design and a general distrust of government development schemes that extended to SBM.

title: Toilet usage situation under SBM in rural West Bengal
text: Coverage figures exceeded 95% by 2018, but roughly half of rural West Bengal was still practising open defecation according to this study, with respondents repeatedly citing comfort. Concludes that construction without behaviour change does not close the usage gap.

title: Sanitation change in rural Jharkhand under SBM
text: Toilet coverage rose from 15% to 85% and open defecation fell from 93% to 26% in the study area. Female community workers were central to local implementation, but construction was prioritised over public education, and NFHS-5 data cited in the study show only 65% actual usage against near-100% official coverage claims.

title: Toilet usage behavior study, rural Bihar households
text: Survey of 653 households. More than a fifth of households that own a toilet still defecate outside, so access is not the whole problem; poor toilet design is also blamed. Bihar started from the worst baseline of any state in SBM's original 2012 survey.

title: After 4 years of Swachh Bharat, toilet use does not match construction spree
text: Based on a survey of about 10,000 people (RICE/Accountability Initiative). Open defecation fell 26 points over four years, but most new toilets used the cheaper single-pit design rather than the recommended twin-pit design, implying manual or costly pit-emptying later. Also reports that some latrines were built under coercion rather than persuasion.

title: Information is key to making India open-defecation-free
text: Argues that open defecation is mainly an information problem rather than an access problem: people often do not know its health risks. Notes that behaviour-change campaigns have relied on coercion rather than persuasion, with modest results.

title: NFHS-5 Data Can Help India Become a Truly Open Defecation Free Country
source_name: The Wire (analysis of NFHS-5 government survey data)
text: Analysis of NFHS-5 data: use of improved sanitation facilities rose from 49% (2015-16) to 70% (2019-21) nationally, in line with SBM's timeline. The authors note a methodological issue: one household member's answer is extrapolated to the whole household, although toilet use varies within households (adults more than children, women more than men), so open defecation is probably undercounted. States needing the most work: Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Ladakh and Manipur.

title: Impact assessment of SBM on acute diarrheal disease outbreaks
text: Secondary source referenced within a broader IJCRT paper. Assesses whether SBM's sanitation push appears in diarrhoeal-disease outbreak data and reports improvement linked to reduced open defecation.

title: Menstrual Hygiene Management in India
text: Explains how menstrual hygiene management was incorporated into SBM's guidelines through the 'Swachh Bharat: Swachh Vidyalaya' school campaign, with the goal of every school having soap, private changing space, water and proper disposal for menstrual products. Describes policy rather than evaluating outcomes.

title: Household sanitation and menstrual hygiene among women in rural Odisha
text: Survey of 700 women in Balasore district. Despite SBM's household sanitation push, women and girls still face barriers including clean water, soap, privacy and disposal that toilet access alone does not solve; sanitation coverage and usable menstrual hygiene facilities are not the same thing.

title: Menstrual health and hygiene practices among female students in Assam
source_name: International Journal of Community Medicine and Public Health
text: Case study from Dibrugarh of menstrual hygiene practices and awareness among female students at one institution. Relates findings to the national MHM guidelines and how they apply in higher-education settings as opposed to schools.

title: Menstrual Hygiene Management Programming in Maharashtra
text: UNICEF field note crediting SBM, described as the country's largest behaviour-change programme, with widening public discussion of menstrual hygiene. Presents Maharashtra as a case where the health, education and sanitation ministries collaborated effectively across sectors, which is not typical.

title: India Menstrual Health Literature Review
text: Literature review covering the 2017 government guidelines on gender issues in SBM(Gramin), including attention to menstrual needs in toilet design and counselling sessions for girls. Describes this as meaningful but incomplete progress, focusing on policy history rather than outcomes.

title: Health, Gender, and Economic Benefits of India's Swachh Bharat Mission
text: Credits SBM's first decade with declines in infant, child and maternal mortality, less stunting, cost savings, fewer school dropouts and better menstrual health. Presents SBM as a model for other countries.

title: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (Clean India Mission)
source_name: UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs
text: UN partnership profile describing a whole-of-government approach in which every ministry had sanitation workplans regardless of mandate, and the mobilisation of more than 600,000 community volunteers ('swachhagrahis').

title: Swachh Bharat Mission 2.0 - Comprehensive Municipal Waste Management in Indian Cities
text: ADB programme document. India generates about 62 million tonnes of municipal solid waste a year, and collection rates in small cities can be under 50%. Credits SBM phase 1 with ending open defecation for about 500 million people but identifies unresolved gaps in legacy waste, plastic and construction-debris management.

title: Waste-Wise Cities: Best Practices in Municipal Solid Waste Management
text: Describes a gap between policy and practice: SBM, AMRUT and Smart Cities together created favourable policy conditions, but practice on the ground (composting, biomethanation and especially plastic recycling) still lags behind policy documents.

title: Global South Nears Waste Tipping Point, World Bank Warns
text: World Bank warning about Global South countries, with India as one case. Credits SBM as the world's largest sanitation initiative but finds urbanisation outpacing infrastructure gains, especially in smaller towns. Identifies cheap multilayer plastic packaging as something formal waste systems are not handling.

title: Swachh Bharat Mission 2.0: Garbage-Free Urban India
text: Exam-preparation summary of the shift from SBM 1.0 (open defecation) to SBM 2.0 ('garbage-free cities'), and the 'waste-to-wealth' framing of composting and biogas. Covers mission terminology and the phase timeline.

title: Government reports urban SBM achievements: star-rated garbage-free cities
text: Coverage of an official statement: four cities (Indore, Ambikapur, Navi Mumbai, Mysuru) achieved 5-star 'garbage-free' status, with dozens more at lower tiers. The 2019 Swachhata Hi Seva campaign had more than 7 crore urban participants and collected a large amount of plastic waste.

title: Solid Waste Management and Contribution of Swachh Bharat Mission in Shimla
source_name: International Journal of Environment and Global Health Research
text: Case study of Shimla's waste collection and disposal challenges, shaped by hill terrain, and how SBM funding and framework fit into local improvements. Largely descriptive.

title: Cabinet approves continuation of Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) till 2025-26
text: Cabinet approval announcement: SBM-Urban 2.0 budget of 1,41,600 crore, over 2.5 times the previous phase. Focus areas: sustaining ODF status, scientific waste processing in all cities, and wastewater management in smaller cities not covered by AMRUT.

title: Jal Shakti ministry targets 2025 for Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen after missing 2024 deadline
text: The original 2024 target for full rural tap-water coverage and 'ODF Plus' status was moved to 2025 after it was missed. About 4 crore rural households remained uncovered at the time of the report. The minister expressed optimism about meeting the new target.

title: Swachh Bharat Mission - Progress and Problems
text: Early-mission briefing (2017). Open defecation fell just over 7 points in the first 16 months but remained above 50% nationally. Toilet coverage figures did not correlate closely with reductions in open defecation across states.

title: Centre releases Rs 1,869 crore for Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen in 2024
source_name: All India Radio / News on Air
text: Funding announcement: over 1,869 crore released as the Centre's share for SBM-Grameen through November 2024, per a Lok Sabha reply, to sustain villages' ODF status.

title: Toward a Menstrual-friendly School Environment
text: Mixed-methods study of school-level menstrual hygiene provisions, set against the 2011 national menstrual hygiene scheme and SBM's guidelines. Focuses on the gap between what guidelines require and what schools deliver day to day.

title: Guidelines on Gender Issues in Sanitation for Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin)
source_name: Ministry of Jal Shakti (Government of India)
text: The 2017 policy document, accessed via the Splash literature review. Requires attention to menstrual hygiene needs in rural toilet design and counselling sessions delivered by qualified staff.

title: 288 people died cleaning sewers, septic tanks in last 3 years: Government
text: Government parliamentary statement reporting 288 deaths from sewer and septic-tank cleaning over three years. Also mentions a 2018-19 national survey that found manual scavengers still working on latrines being converted to SBM's sanitary standard.

title: Two sanitation workers die cleaning sewage shaft at Noida house
text: Single-incident report: two migrant workers from West Bengal, hired informally to clean a residential septic tank in Noida, died from gas inhalation.
